title: Domain Knowledge Graph Construction Pipeline with Relation Extraction & Cypher Graph Reasoning Engine
problem: Unstructured technical and biomedical literature contains deeply interconnected entities that cannot be queried through keyword search or basic vector retrieval without losing relational context. Naive information extraction pipelines produce noisy entity boundaries, unresolved synonyms, and disconnected graph fragments. This project builds an automated knowledge graph construction and reasoning pipeline in Python. The system processes unstructured corpora using spaCy and BERT relation extractors, normalizes entities against canonical ontologies, persists nodes and directed edges in Neo4j, and executes Cypher reasoning queries over multi-hop relationships with interactive D3.js topology visualization.

use_cases.title: Biomedical Literature Target Discovery Engines
use_cases.first_sentence: Life sciences research laboratories need to uncover latent connections between molecular compounds, target proteins, and clinical adverse reactions from thousands of published papers.
use_cases.second_sentence: The pipeline ingests biomedical abstract batches, extracts normalized gene-disease associations, and enables researchers to execute 3-hop traversal queries identifying drug repurposing candidates.

use_cases.title: Regulatory Compliance & Corporate Ownership Auditing
use_cases.first_sentence: Financial risk analysts must detect undisclosed beneficial ownership chains and conflicts of interest across thousands of corporate filings and legal contracts.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system constructs an entity-relationship graph linking holding companies, subsidiaries, and executive board members, evaluating structural circular ownership loops.

use_cases.title: Technical Architecture Dependency & Incident Mapping
use_cases.first_sentence: Cloud infrastructure platform teams need clear visual and programmatic representations of distributed service dependencies, APIs, and shared datastores.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine parses post-mortem incident documentation and architecture RFCs, synthesizing a queryable dependency graph that highlights cascading single points of failure.

hard_parts: Extracting complex overlapping relation triplets from dense academic literature with high precision
Resolving entity aliases and polysemy to canonical ontology identifiers without introducing duplicate entity nodes
Modeling high-performance property graph schemas in Neo4j with optimized indexes for recursive multi-hop traversals
Designing deterministic graph reasoning queries that infer hidden transitive links and circular path anomalies
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase separating text extraction pipelines, entity resolution modules, and Neo4j graph access layers
Quantitative extraction benchmark reporting precision, recall, and F1 scores against human-annotated entity relationship datasets
Anti-fake verification script inserting unseen dynamic text passages and asserting automated creation of verified canonical nodes and edges in Neo4j

components.name: Corpus Ingestion & spaCy Linguistic Parser
components.purpose: Ingests raw text documents, segments sentences, and extracts syntactic dependency trees

components.name: Transformer Entity & Relation Extraction Engine
components.purpose: Classifies named entity spans and predicts directed relationship predicates between entity pairs

components.name: Entity Resolution & Ontology Linker
components.purpose: Normalizes textual mentions to canonical ontology concepts using string similarity and taxonomic entity lookups

components.name: Neo4j Property Graph Persistence Layer
components.purpose: Batches entity and relationship insertions using Cypher statements with uniqueness constraints and indexes

components.name: Multi-Hop Graph Reasoning & Cypher Query Engine
components.purpose: Executes declarative graph traversal queries inferring transitive relationships and structural anomalies

components.name: Interactive D3.js Graph Topology Visualizer
components.purpose: Renders browser-based interactive force-directed graph diagrams with node filtering and neighborhood zoom

architecture.data_flow: Unstructured text documents enter the ingestion parser; spaCy extracts sentences and linguistic dependency features; the BERT relation extractor identifies entity spans and predicts semantic relationships; the entity resolver maps entity strings to canonical ontology identifiers via the Wikidata API; resolved nodes and relationship edges stream to the Neo4j persistence layer in batched Cypher transactions; the reasoning engine executes multi-hop traversals over the constructed property graph; the results stream to the D3.js frontend for interactive visual analysis.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Neo4j schema constraints enforcing uniqueness on canonical entity IDs; relation confidence thresholds filtering low-probability extraction predictions.

targets.metric: Named Entity Recognition and Relation Extraction F1 Score
targets.method: Micro-averaged F1 score evaluated against gold-standard annotated relation extraction evaluation corpus
targets.input: 500 annotated scientific abstract sentences containing 1,500 ground-truth entity relation triplets
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Python 3.11 with HuggingFace transformers pipeline
targets.minimum_pass: Relation extraction micro-F1 score is >= 0.74 across 500 test sentences
targets.target: Relation extraction micro-F1 score is >= 0.84 across 500 test sentences
targets.report: Information extraction precision, recall, and F1 score evaluation report

targets.metric: Neo4j Knowledge Graph Multi-Hop Query Latency
targets.method: Execution timing for recursive 3-hop traversal Cypher queries discovering indirect relationships between entities
targets.input: 100 benchmark multi-hop graph queries executed against constructed 50,000-node property graph
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, 8GB RAM, Neo4j Community Edition in Docker
targets.minimum_pass: p95 query response time for 3-hop graph traversals is < 45 milliseconds
targets.target: p95 query response time for 3-hop graph traversals is < 18 milliseconds
targets.report: Neo4j Cypher query latency profiling and execution timing log

targets.method: Accuracy of linking text surface mentions to correct canonical Wikidata identifiers
targets.input: 300 polysemous and abbreviated entity mentions across clinical and technical text
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, local offline ontology index or Wikidata API mock cache
targets.minimum_pass: Linking precision is >= 82.0% across 300 entity mentions
targets.target: Linking precision is >= 91.5% across 300 entity mentions
targets.report: Entity resolution evaluation summary and disambiguation accuracy report

prerequisites: Proficiency in Python programming, transformer NLP models (HuggingFace/BERT), and spaCy linguistic parsing
Understanding of graph databases (Neo4j, Cypher query syntax) and relational knowledge representation

environment.ram: 8GB RAM (16GB recommended for running local Neo4j Docker container and BERT inference)
environment.gpu: None required (quantized DistilBERT or lightweight relation extraction models run on CPU)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source stack using Neo4j Community Edition and HuggingFace models)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Docker Desktop (Neo4j 5 Community container) and Python 3.11
environment.fallback_path: NetworkX in-memory graph representation with JSON persistence if Docker or Neo4j is unavailable

riskiest_component.name: Relation Extraction Precision Degradation on Complex Sentence Structures
riskiest_component.mitigation: Utilize dependency parse path filtering alongside transformer relation heads, applying probability cutoff thresholds.
riskiest_component.fallback: Rule-based Hearst pattern and dependency tree extractors for high-confidence relation subsets.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an automated knowledge graph construction pipeline in Python with spaCy/BERT relation extraction, Neo4j persistence, and D3.js visualization.
worksheet.q2: Target users: life science researchers, compliance auditors, and data platform engineers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: biomedical literature discovery, regulatory ownership auditing, and technical architecture dependency mapping.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 40 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 35 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 40.25 -> 40 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: overlapping relation extraction, entity alias resolution to Wikidata ontologies, high-performance Cypher property graph modeling, and sub-45ms multi-hop traversals.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 5,000 scientific abstracts, gold-standard annotated benchmark relations, and ontology dictionaries. Public scientific abstracts only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: NetworkX in-memory graph representation.

worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; public scientific abstracts only, zero private biomedical patient data.
